MIKE McCARTHY IS PITTSBURGH'S HEAD COACH, NOT MIKE TOMLIN. Tomlin stepped down in January 2026 after 19 seasons and McCarthy replaced him; Tomlin is now an NBC analyst, which is why he is the one calling it a dumpster fire on television. McCarthy coached Rodgers for thirteen years in Green Bay. Do not mix them up on air - it is the easiest mistake in this story.

THERE IS NO FULL PUBLIC TRANSCRIPT OF THE McAFEE INTERVIEW. Every Rodgers quote in Block 1 is as transcribed by ESPN and CBS Sports off the live broadcast. The two outlets independently agree on the key lines, which is why they are in here, but say "as transcribed by ESPN" once at the top of the segment and do not present them as a verbatim transcript.

"RELEASED" OR "WAIVED" - BOTH ARE CORRECT AND IT WILL SOUND LIKE AN ERROR. Steelers.com says released; ESPN says waived. Because the move came after the trade deadline, even a vested veteran passes through waivers. He cleared them Thursday at 4 PM with no claim and is an unrestricted free agent.

THE ROONEY QUOTE HAS TWO PUBLISHED WORDINGS. The Post-Gazette, whose own reporter did the interview, has "insubordination will not be tolerated." ESPN has "insubordination can't be tolerated." Use the Post-Gazette version.

THE GRIEVANCE HAS NOT BEEN FILED. ESPN reports only that Pittsburgh may file for conduct detrimental to recover the $8.56 million. Do not say they are doing it. And Joel Corry's roughly $6.1 million figure is the maximum allowable discipline as a calculation, not a reported settlement.

TWO MONEY ITEMS ARE RUMOR-TIER AND STAY OFF THE AIR: an aggregated Ari Meirov item about a "$22,000,000 issue" tied to Rodgers not reporting to the facility, and reported comments from his brother Jordan and his estranged father, neither of which could be verified.

RODGERS HAS SAID NOTHING SINCE THE RELEASE - no statement, no post, no podcast, as of Friday afternoon, and no response to Rooney calling him insubordinate. If something lands overnight this block changes. Note he had already announced on May 20 that he would retire after this season, so retirement is not news, it is the standing plan.

USE THE CAREER NUMBERS FROM STEELERS.COM AND NFL.COM: 68,515 yards, 543 touchdowns, 274 games, 267 starts, 22 seasons. Wikipedia's Aaron Rodgers page is stale to Week 2 and shows 66,682 and 528 while still listing him as an active Steeler. Do not read those.

KALSHI IS A PREDICTION MARKET, NOT A SPORTSBOOK, and the two markets disagree about his next team: Kalshi has retirement at 74 percent with Baltimore second among teams; BetOnline posted no retirement line at all and has Cleveland second. Name the market every time.
BILL COWHER, RUSSELL WILSON AND NATE BURLESON were reported to have "struck a similar tone" on CBS with no direct quotes published. Do not put words in Cowher's mouth.

ESPN'S STEELERS PLAYOFF PERCENTAGES LOOK WRONG. The same piece carries a division figure falling from 19.7 percent to about 5 percent and separately 92 percent with a Denver win and 82 percent with a loss. Those cannot both be right for a 6-4 team. Use the 19.7-to-5 division number or nothing. RODGERS-STORY STALE PAGES, AND THERE ARE A LOT: an SI piece dated Nov 24, 2025 describes a 6-5 Steelers team after a loss to Chicago and will read exactly like this week - it is last year. THE ENTIRE FRIDAY NFL INJURY REPORT. nfl.com/injuries and Sharp Football's all-32 report both show "No designation" in the game status column for every player in every Sunday game and the Monday game. TWO QUARTERBACKS WHO MAY NOT PLAY SUNDAY AND HAVE ALREADY MOVED THE BOARD. YAHOO'S WEEK 12 INJURY TRACKER LISTS QUENTON NELSON AS OUT UNDER THE SEATTLE SEAHAWKS. Nelson is an Indianapolis guard. The entry is mislabeled and appears to be propagating to at least one other outlet. Do not read it.

hours.subtitle: Aaron Rodgers cold open, 20 minutes (8:00-8:20), then college football (8:20-9:00)

blocks.title: Block 1: Cold Open - Aaron Rodgers Is Gone

segments.title: The release, and the money

items.h: Pittsburgh released Aaron Rodgers Wednesday and the team's entire official statement was one sentence
items.t: Steelers.com posted it at 4:48 PM Wednesday Nov 25, bylined Teresa Varley: "The Steelers released quarterback Aaron Rodgers." No coach quoted, no executive quoted, no reason given. Gerry Dulac at the Post-Gazette had it first.

items.h: "Released" or "waived" - both are right, and it will sound like an error
items.t: Steelers.com says released; ESPN says waived. Because the move came after the trade deadline, even a vested veteran passes through waivers. He cleared them Thursday at 4 PM with no claim and is now an unrestricted free agent who can sign anywhere for the rest of the season.

items.h: The contract: one year, $22,502,750, and Pittsburgh still owes $8.56 million guaranteed
items.t: His second straight one-year Pittsburgh deal, worth up to $25 million with incentives including $625,000 per playoff win at 75 percent of snaps. He has been paid $13.44 million. Per ESPN's Dan Graziano the release does not change their 2026 cap number at all.

items.h: The live wire: ESPN reports Pittsburgh MAY file a grievance for conduct detrimental
items.t: If it succeeded they would get the $8.56 million back as a cap credit at season's end. Joel Corry's math on maximum discipline - a one-week fine plus a four-week unpaid suspension - is about $6.1 million. Say that is a hypothetical ceiling, not a settlement, and say ESPN reports only that they could file, not that they have.

items.h: He turns 43 next Wednesday, Dec 2
items.t: And he had already announced on May 20 that he would retire after this season - so retirement is not news, it is the standing plan.

segments.title: What he actually said on Pat McAfee's show - this is the segment

items.h: Frame the sourcing first, one sentence
items.t: There is no full public transcript. Every quote here is as transcribed by ESPN and CBS Sports off the live broadcast Wednesday midday, and the two outlets independently agree on the key lines. McAfee teased it beforehand with two words: "This feels large."

items.h: He found out he was benched from a teammate, not from the coach
items.t: Rodgers: "I was talking to Muth and a couple other guys and he said, 'I can't believe they're doing this.'" And Rodgers answered: "Doing what?" Muth is tight end Pat Freiermuth.

items.h: The allegation that made it a national story - he said the head coach fell asleep in a quarterback meeting
items.t: "Mike came in late, sat down, and within 10 minutes began snoring. Woke himself up, was rattling his papers. We all looked around." And: "I'm telling you, you snored in the meeting twice, in a quarterback meeting; that's unacceptable." He says McCarthy answered: "You're telling me you've never slept at a facility before."

items.h: And the one McCarthy himself confirmed, which is why it matters most
items.t: At halftime of the Eagles loss, Rodgers says McCarthy broke the huddle on "All right, one, two, three, Packers." Rodgers: "And I think the nail in the coffin for so many of us was at halftime." And: "Everybody across the entire locker room heard it." On preparation: "I think he learns the plan during the week."

items.h: The line that decides whether you defend him
items.t: "I'm not saying that to bury you." And: "I'm saying that because this behavior and these habits are not healthy." And: "I have a hundred witnesses and collaborating people who would support what I'm saying." And: "I'm standing on the truth. Everybody there knows it." Multiple outlets report he called McCarthy "unwell" and suggested a health issue - that is the part that got him released, not the snoring.

items.h: The Green Bay callback - and McCarthy coached him thirteen years there
items.t: "Nobody knew what was going on for 10 years in Green Bay." And: "Everybody knows. Just like the guys in Green Bay knew."

items.h: He did not touch his teammates, and he saw the release coming
items.t: "I love those guys. I talked to so many of them. They know what's going on." He thanked Mike Tomlin by name for "giving me that joy and passion back." And: "What's the repercussions for me? I don't care about getting released. I don't care about making any more money." And: "That ship has definitely sailed. I'm not going back to Pittsburgh."

items.h: Do not skip the corroboration - it is the fairest thing in the segment
items.t: ESPN's Brooke Pryor had a source say of the allegations: "It's all true." ESPN's Adam Schefter had a source say McCarthy "crossed" Rodgers. And NFL Network's Jane Slater reported several sources raised similar concerns about McCarthy during his Dallas years. The counter-witness: retired quarterback Ben DiNucci, two and a half years with McCarthy in Dallas, says he "never witnessed him doze off or fall asleep."

segments.title: Pittsburgh's answer - and the man who used to have the job

items.h: Art Rooney II went on the record Thursday and was not careful about it
items.t: To Gerry Dulac, whose own reporter did the interview, so use this wording: "Insubordination will not be tolerated." And: "When you start getting ultimatums, you can't live with that." And the one that will get the phones going: "He talks about wanting to be a good teammate, but you don't do that to your teammates a couple days before the game." ESPN renders the first as "insubordination can't be tolerated" - use the Post-Gazette version.

items.h: The ultimatum itself, per Post-Gazette sources
items.t: Rodgers told McCarthy: "Either let me call all the plays or just release me." Rapoport and Garafolo reported a floated compromise where quarterbacks coach Tom Arth would relay plays to him. Rooney's position is that this is outside a player's job description, full stop.

items.h: Rooney guaranteed the coach's job on the same day - ask whether that is confidence or damage control
items.t: To ESPN in writing: "I am disappointed in where this went with Aaron Rodgers, but I have 100% confidence in Mike McCarthy." And to the Post-Gazette, that he expects McCarthy to be the coach "this season, next season and beyond."

items.h: McCarthy, Wednesday: it was his call, and he gave up an admission that will follow him
items.t: "There was an ultimatum made clearly outside of his job description. So, it was my decision to bench him." He disputed the no-communication claim. He confirmed the halftime moment as "an embarrassing moment, but I just think we worked a lot of hours, so definitely a difference of opinion." He defended himself with "I know how to win, and that's the facts. This is my third program." And: "I probably should have had more dialogue earlier in the process when I first arrived here." Per CBS he did not address the snoring specifically.

items.h: Mike McCarthy is Pittsburgh's head coach, not Mike Tomlin - do not mix them up
items.t: Tomlin stepped down in January 2026 after 19 seasons and McCarthy replaced him. Rodgers says he vouched for McCarthy in Pittsburgh's coaching search.

items.h: And Tomlin, now an NBC analyst, called it a dumpster fire on Thanksgiving
items.t: At halftime of Chiefs-Bills, to Mike Tirico: "I'm upset about it, it's a dumpster fire." And: "Sad that we might be looking at the end of a legendary career." And: "He was beloved, and I'm not over-exaggerating that."

items.h: The locker room is shellshocked, and the detail tells you everything
items.t: ESPN's Brooke Pryor reports "confusion and discontent" and that Steelers sources backed Rodgers' account. Freiermuth: "Obviously, he said what he said," and on confidence in the staff, just "I'm confident." Rookie quarterback Drew Allar: "It's kind of sad to see because I have a lot of respect for Aaron" - and safety DeShon Elliott was trying to signal him to stop talking to reporters. Marquez Valdes-Scantling, a former Packers teammate: "I think he's the best player that ever played the game at that position."

segments.title: Where he goes, and the panel

items.h: Say the fact first - he has not signed anywhere and nobody has been reported to have called
items.t: ESPN's Jeremy Fowler reports the Patriots and Eagles are unlikely to show interest, and that Baltimore - who plays Pittsburgh twice - might consider it but probably will not. An unnamed AFC executive told ESPN playoff-bubble teams might get desperate but "it will be hard after his comments."

items.h: Retirement is the favorite, and the two markets disagree about the teams
items.t: On Kalshi, a prediction market and not a sportsbook, retires-or-no-team is 74 percent, with New England 14, Baltimore 7, Pittsburgh 4, Atlanta 2. BetOnline posted team odds with no retirement line at all: Patriots +200, Browns +300, Falcons +400, Giants +500. Name the market every time - Baltimore is second on Kalshi and absent from BetOnline; Cleveland is second on BetOnline and absent from Kalshi.

items.h: Gronkowski on FOX: "To me personally, I don't think he plays again in the NFL"
items.t: And the other published odds board, for contrast.

items.h: The milestones he is now stranded short of - the closing beat
items.t: 68,515 yards, fifth all-time, and he needs about 1,712 more for 70,000 - he finishes roughly 1,485 short. 543 touchdowns, third all-time behind only Brady and Brees. 296 games, four short of 300. Four MVPs, one Super Bowl, 22 seasons.

items.h: PANEL: whistleblower or saboteur? Give everybody a turn.
items.t: For him: Pryor's source said "it's all true," Schefter's source said the coach crossed him, Slater found the same concerns in Dallas, McCarthy admitted the halftime moment, James Harrison said he had heard such things before, Ryan Clark said "not 1 lie told." Against him: T.J. Lang, eight years his teammate in Green Bay, said "I think it's despicable" and "it's a victim mentality"; Greg Jennings said "none of us ever saw that"; Brady said "the sanctity of an NFL locker room is a very sacred place"; and Terry Bradshaw, four Super Bowls in that building, said "I'm sorry that he had to go public with all his gripes and complaints." And Le'Veon Bell splits it perfectly - believes about 98 percent of it and still thinks it was selfish.

items.h: The hand-off to the board
items.t: A 6-4 team holding the AFC's last wild-card spot just handed the ball to a 31-year-old with one pass attempt all season, with two men who have never played an NFL regular-season down behind him. That game kicked off Friday afternoon - Topic 14 has it.

blocks.title: Block 2: College - The Carnage and the Two Rankings

segments.title: Last Saturday: three of the top ten lost, two in overtime

items.t: UCLA's first loss of the season, and it cost UCLA its starting quarterback. ESPN's schedule page says 3OT; one liveblog says only OT.

items.h: Washington 27, No. 8 Indiana 24 in overtime
items.t: Decided by a missed Indiana field goal. Washington then showed up in the committee's top 25 for the first time.

items.h: No. 10 BYU 31, Kansas 29 in three overtimes
items.t: BYU survived and stayed alive for the Big 12 title game.

items.h: Nebraska 31, No. 14 Ohio State 28
items.t: Ohio State's second straight loss. It fell from AP 16 to AP 25 and hosts Michigan today as a ten-point favorite.

items.h: San Diego State 22, No. 17 Boise State 20
items.t: The result that blew up the Group of Six playoff race, and Boise State still holds the automatic bid.

items.h: Missouri 28, No. 16 Kentucky 14, and Navy 38, Memphis 34
items.t: Kentucky and Memphis both fell out of the AP poll entirely. Missouri is now ranked by both systems and hosts Oklahoma today.

items.h: Rutgers 25, Penn State 24; Arizona 35, Kansas State 28 (OT); Oklahoma State 30, Arizona State 27 (OT)
items.t: Three more one-score finishes, two of them in overtime.

items.h: The chalk that mattered
items.t: Georgia 34, South Carolina 6. Utah 38, TCU 17. Alabama 47, Chattanooga 0. Texas 45, Arkansas 3 (Arch Manning 287 and three scores). Notre Dame 24, SMU 3. Miami 28, Virginia Tech 20. Tennessee 27, LSU 13. Wake Forest 50, Georgia Tech 29. Texas Tech 20, Baylor 10. Oregon 45, Michigan State 7. Oklahoma 28, Texas A&M 7. NC State 28, Florida State 10.

items.h: PANEL: which of the three top-ten losses actually changes the playoff?
items.t: UCLA lost and still clinches the Big Ten with a win today. Indiana lost and fell six spots with the committee. Ohio State lost and moved up with the AP. Make the case.

items.h: 11 through 25

items.h: The falls are the story
items.t: UCLA 4 to 10. Indiana 6 to 12. Boise State 15 to 22. And Ohio State 16 to 25, a nine-spot drop on a second straight loss. New in: Oklahoma 19, Missouri 24. Out: Kentucky and Memphis.

items.h: Unlike the last two weeks, we have records, points and first-place votes
items.t: They are quotable this morning. Say the poll came out Sunday, not Monday.

segments.title: The fourth CFP rankings, out Tuesday night Nov 24

items.h: No Group of Six team is anywhere in the committee's top 25 for the first time this season
items.t: Not Boise State, not Liberty, not UTSA, not New Mexico. Meanwhile the AP ranks Liberty 21st at 10-1 and Boise State 22nd at 9-2. One system has them on the board and the other cannot see them at all.

items.h: The CFP top 12
items.t: 1 Georgia (10-1), 2 Utah (11-0), 3 Texas (9-2), 4 Notre Dame (10-1), 5 Tennessee (9-2), 6 Alabama (9-2), 7 Miami (10-1), 8 Wake Forest (10-1), 9 UCLA (10-1), 10 BYU (9-2), 11 Texas Tech (10-1), 12 Oregon (8-3).

items.h: 13 through 25

items.h: The single-team splits worth naming
items.t: Ohio State is CFP 21 and AP 25 - the committee likes a four-loss Ohio State more than the voters do. Miami is AP 4 and CFP 7.

Oregon is squeezed out by a Boise State team the committee will not rank, because the G6 bid goes to the highest-ranked G6 team whether or not it cracks the 25. Final bracket lands Sunday Dec 6.

items.t: Liberty and UTSA are both +700, New Mexico +1000, Louisiana Tech +1200.

blocks.title: Block 3: West Virginia - It Was Decided Last Night

segments.title: Houston 34, West Virginia 31

items.h: Jonathan Dimas hit a 23-yarder as the clock ran out
items.t: Houston tied it 31-31 on Makhi Hughes' 3-yard run with 5:25 left. Senior Day, the home finale, 37,380 at Milan Puskar, on TNT.

items.h: The turn: Jack Cassidy missed a 42-yard field goal that would have made it a 13-point lead
items.t: Hughes answered with a 71-yard run. Rodriguez afterward: "If I had it to do over again, I would have gone for it and not tried for the field goal." And: "This game was there for the taking."

items.h: Michael Hawkins Jr. was hurt in the fourth quarter with the game tied and did not return
items.t: Scotty Fox Jr. finished it. That injury is the reason last night at Utah looked the way it did.

items.h: 490 to 459 in total yards and neither team turned it over once
items.t: Hughes 19 carries, 158 yards, three touchdowns. Keisean Henderson, a true freshman starting for an injured Conner Weigman, 18-of-28 for 268. Cam Cook 25 carries for 131 and a score - a week after getting 12 yards on nine carries against Kansas.

items.h: Hawkins is the first player in West Virginia history with 2,000 passing and 1,000 rushing yards in a season
items.t: He went 13-of-24 for 130 with a touchdown and ran for 98 more plus his 21st rushing touchdown of the year. On a 5-6 team, that is the season in one sentence.

items.h: Records after: Houston 8-3 (5-3), West Virginia 5-6 (2-6) on a three-game losing streak
items.t: WVU went into last night not bowl eligible.

segments.title: West Virginia at No. 2 Utah, last night, 9:00 ET on FOX - GET THE SCORE FIRST

items.h: This sheet was built before kickoff. There is no result in it.
items.t: The Big 12's own page listed the game as upcoming with no result as of Friday. Pull the box score before you open the mic.

items.h: The stake was the entire season
items.t: West Virginia was 5-6 and not bowl eligible. Beat an 11-0 Utah team on the road or finish 5-7 with a third straight losing season.

items.h: Utah went from -20.5 to -26.5 in five days
items.t: DraftKings opened Utah -20.5 with a 69.5 on Nov 22 and was -26.5 with a 66.5 by Nov 27. Six points toward Utah, three points off the total. theScore Bet had -25.5 on Nov 24. The driver was the quarterback.

items.h: Hawkins was listed doubtful on the Big 12 injury report late Tuesday
items.t: Scotty Fox Jr. was in line to start. Rodriguez Tuesday: "He's questionable right now. He didn't do anything yesterday. He won't do anything today." And: "It's a shorter week, too, so that's the other challenge."

items.h: The frame Rodriguez chose, and it is the best thing he has said all year
items.t: "I don't even look at it as far as spoiling someone else's season." "You get to play for a bowl game against the No. 2 ranked team in the country in a great environment." "You get a chance to prove yourselves on national TV again." And to close on: "It's everything a college player would want." These are the only traceable Rodriguez quotes of the week.

items.h: On Utah's defense, same interview
items.t: "They'll outnumber you. They'll pressure you on every down and distance." "They play a lot of man coverage, so on third down they'll come from wherever."

items.h: Utah's side: 11-0, the last unbeaten in the sport, and already into the Big 12 title game
items.t: Devon Dampier is the No. 2 Heisman price at +500.

blocks.title: Block 4: Rivalry Week - The Board and Picks

segments.title: Thursday and Friday - six games finished before we went on

items.h: Thursday: TCU at No. 11/9 Texas Tech, 8:00 ESPN
items.t: Texas Tech -14 with a 46.5 on DraftKings Nov 27; it opened -11.5 on Nov 22. Texas Tech clinched the Big 12 title game with a win - check that first.

items.h: No. 3/5 Texas at Texas A&M, Friday 7:30 ABC - a top-five team on the road
items.t: Texas -11.5 with a 40.5 (DraftKings Nov 27; -10.5 on Nov 24). Texas needed this win plus help to reach the SEC title game.

items.h: No. 25 Nebraska at No. 13 Iowa, Friday noon CBS
items.t: Iowa -3.5 with a 40.5 (DraftKings Nov 27; -4.5 on Nov 24). Ranked-vs-ranked only on the committee's board - the AP does not rank Nebraska at all.

items.h: No. 20 Florida at Florida State, Friday 3:30 ABC
items.t: Florida -6.5 with a 53.5 (DraftKings Nov 27). Ignore CBS's table on this one, it has the home team wrong.

items.h: Also Friday
items.t: Mississippi State at No. 22/23 Ole Miss, noon ABC, Ole Miss -18.5 with a 56.5. Minnesota at Wisconsin, 7:30 NBC, Wisconsin -7.5 with a 37.5.

items.h: Four league titles were decided Friday afternoon
items.t: Tulsa at UTSA, noon ESPN, UTSA -1.5 - UTSA clinched the American with a win. Toledo at Ohio, noon ESPNU, Toledo -3 - winner goes to the MAC title game. Buffalo at Akron, noon CBSSN, Buffalo -7.5 - Buffalo also clinched the MAC with a win. Air Force at New Mexico, 4:30 on The CW, New Mexico -6.5 - New Mexico clinched the Mountain West with a win, and a five-way tie at the top goes to composite computer rankings.

segments.title: The honest shape of today's board

items.h: There is exactly one true ranked-vs-ranked game in the Saturday window on both boards
items.t: And it decides the Big Ten.

items.h: No. 15 USC at No. 9 UCLA, 3:30 on CBS - UCLA clinches the Big Ten title game with a win
items.t: USC -7 with a 45.5 (DraftKings Nov 22 and Nov 24; theScore Bet -7.5, CBS -6.5). CFP 15 at CFP 9, AP 15 at AP 10. A 10-1 UCLA team that just lost in triple overtime and lost its starting quarterback is a seven-point home underdog to a three-loss crosstown rival. That is the game of the day.

items.h: No. 24 Washington at No. 12 Oregon, 7:30 on NBC
items.t: Oregon -13.5 with a 49.5 (DraftKings Nov 22; -14 on Nov 24). Oregon is first out of the playoff field and needs a win plus help for the Big Ten game - and Washington just beat Indiana in overtime. The AP does not rank Washington, so do not call it ranked-vs-ranked on an AP basis.

items.h: No. 17 Oklahoma at No. 23 Missouri, 4:15 on SEC Network
items.t: Missouri -1.5 with a 41.5 (DraftKings Nov 22; others at -2 and -2.5). The lowest spread on any ranked-vs-ranked game today, two 7-4 teams the AP also ranks at 19 and 24.

items.h: Only two top-ten teams are on the road
items.t: No. 4/3 Notre Dame at Syracuse, noon on ABC, Notre Dame -25.5 with a 53.5 (DraftKings Nov 27). No. 5/7 Tennessee at Vanderbilt, 7:00 on ESPN, Tennessee -13.5 with a 43.5 - and Tennessee needs this win plus a Texas loss to reach Atlanta.

items.h: The spot to circle: Michigan at No. 21/25 Ohio State, noon on FOX
items.t: Ohio State -10 with a 37.5 (DraftKings Nov 27; -10.5 with a 38.5 on Nov 22). A four-loss Ohio State team on a two-game losing streak is giving ten to a Michigan team that just beat UCLA in triple overtime, and the total is one of the lowest on the board. Ohio State's Big Ten path is the longest in the league: beat Michigan, get Maryland, Rutgers and Wisconsin to win, and get Indiana, Iowa, Oregon and USC all to lose.

segments.title: The rivalries, the Heisman and the carousel - fast rundown

items.h: Auburn at No. 6 Alabama, the Iron Bowl, 7:30 on ABC
items.t: Alabama -15.5 with a 49.5 (DraftKings Nov 22 and Nov 24; consensus -16.5). Alabama's SEC path requires beating Auburn plus losses from both Tennessee and Texas.

items.h: Georgia Tech at No. 1 Georgia, Clean Old-Fashioned Hate, 3:30 on ABC
items.t: Georgia -35.5 with a 55.5, and three separate sources agree on both numbers. The biggest spread on the board.

items.h: South Carolina at Clemson, the Palmetto Bowl, 3:00 on ESPN2 - South Carolina is favored
items.t: South Carolina -4 on DraftKings Nov 22 and -5.5 on Nov 24. CBS's table says Clemson -4.5 while CBS's own text says South Carolina by 5.5 on the road. Two DraftKings captures both have South Carolina favored.

items.h: Purdue at No. 14/12 Indiana, the Old Oaken Bucket, 7:00 on FS1
items.t: Indiana -22.5 with a 52.5, unanimous across sources.

items.h: Arizona State at No. 16 Arizona, the Territorial Cup, 9:00 on FOX - do not quote the total
items.t: Arizona -7.5. Four sources give four totals: 55.5, 54.5, 53.5 and 49.5. That is a six-point spread on one number.

items.h: There is no Bedlam and no Notre Dame-Stanford this year
items.t: Oklahoma is at Missouri, Oklahoma State hosts Kansas at 6:15 on ESPN2, Notre Dame is at Syracuse and Stanford hosts SMU at 3:30 on ACCN. Say it before somebody calls in.

items.h: Virginia at Virginia Tech, 3:00 on The CW, and NC State at North Carolina, noon on ACCN
items.t: Virginia Tech -3; North Carolina -6 on DraftKings Nov 27.

items.h: The Big 12 and ACC closers
items.t: Cincinnati at No. 10/11 BYU, 3:30 FOX, BYU -14 - BYU needs a win plus a Texas Tech loss. Baylor at No. 18/17 Houston, 9:30 ESPN2, Houston -4.5. Duke at No. 8 Wake Forest, 3:30 ESPN, Wake -14, and the ACC title game is already set: Miami versus Wake Forest. Boston College at No. 7/4 Miami, noon ESPN, Miami -24.5.

items.h: The SEC closers
items.t: No. 19/18 Louisville at Kentucky, the Governor's Cup, noon ESPN2, Louisville -3. LSU at Arkansas, the Golden Boot, 12:45 SECN, LSU -14.5 with a 49.5. Penn State at Maryland, 3:30 FS1, Penn State -7.5.

items.h: The highest total on the entire board: No. 22 Boise State at Colorado State, 6:00 on USA
items.t: Boise -21 with a 75.5. The team holding a playoff bid the committee will not rank is in a seventy-five-and-a-half-point game.

items.h: The Heisman favorite's team has lost two in a row and he is pulling away anyway
items.t: Jeremiah Smith, the Ohio State receiver, went from -140 at FanDuel on Nov 15 to -400 on a Nov 22 board to an 80 percent implied price on a prediction market Nov 25. Three boards, three books - name the book and the date.

items.h: Behind him
items.t: Devon Dampier of 11-0 Utah is the clear No. 2 at +500. Darian Mensah of Miami has collapsed from +350 to +1550. Gio Lopez of Wake Forest came from +6000 to +3000. CJ Carr and Gunner Stockton are both +3500. No named-sportsbook board was captured Thursday or Friday.

items.h: TCU fired Sonny Dykes on Nov 22 - and he signed a multiyear extension seven months ago
items.t: He was 41-23 over five seasons; the Utah loss dropped TCU to 5-6.

items.h: Florida State hired Georgia defensive coordinator Glenn Schumann on a five-year deal
items.t: He replaces Mike Norvell, fired after a Week 9 home loss.

items.h: Eastern Michigan and Chris Creighton parted ways Nov 25 after 13 seasons
items.t: The school calls it mutual; one outlet calls it a firing. Use the school's language. Open jobs on CBS's tracker: Maryland, Baylor, TCU, UTEP, Sam Houston, Arkansas State, Eastern Michigan.

items.h: The Deion Sanders item is a rumor and must be said that way
items.t: A former On3 reporter relaying an anonymous source, written up by HEAVY, republished by Yahoo early Friday, says Colorado intends to move on from Sanders after today's UCF game regardless of result, with New Mexico's Jason Eck the leading candidate. Colorado has said nothing and Sanders has publicly dismissed hot-seat talk. Colorado hosts UCF at 2:00 on TNT.

segments.title: Picks and the tease

items.h: One college play and one sentence from each panelist
items.t: Name the book and the date you are taking. These are Nov 22 to Nov 27 DraftKings numbers, not live ones.

items.h: The framing
items.t: One ranked-versus-ranked game all day and it decides the Big Ten, with a 10-1 UCLA team a seven-point home dog in it. To be a hero today you take a side on USC at UCLA, on Michigan getting ten at Ohio State, or on Missouri as a one-and-a-half-point favorite over Oklahoma.

items.h: Tease
items.t: Trent at the top of the hour, the Thanksgiving triple-header where all three games were won inside the final minute, and that Aaron Rodgers was released on Wednesday.

hours.title: Hour 2
hours.subtitle: Trent Conner's fantasy five at the top, then NFL Week 12 (9:00-10:00)

segments.title: Five minutes, hard out - four beats and no more

items.h: Open with the week and the byes, thirty seconds
items.t: This is Week 12 and it started Wednesday. Zero teams are on bye - all 32 play. And the thing people must act on: Week 13 byes are the Ravens, Colts, Raiders and Jets, so anybody streaming Brissett, Richardson, Mendoza or Geno Smith needs a Week 13 plan right now.

items.h: Skip Rodgers here - he got twenty minutes off the top. Just the fantasy line on Pittsburgh.
items.t: Mason Rudolph started Friday with one pass attempt all season behind him, and Will Howard and Drew Allar, who have never played an NFL regular-season down, are behind him.

items.h: The Colts waived Daniel Jones and named Anthony Richardson the starter
items.t: His first start since 2024 - and that is why the Giants defense is a stream of the week.

items.h: Drake Maye has a fractured fibula and is out at least six weeks; Tommy DeVito starts
items.t: No surgery, not on IR. Vrabel: "Tommy's our starter." DeVito took four sacks and an interception in his last outing, which makes the Chargers defense FantasyPros' No. 1 stream.

items.h: Must-start with the number: Jacory Croskey-Merritt, Washington, at Arizona
items.t: He has scored 12.6 PPR or more in every game with 15-plus touches; Arizona has allowed the ninth-most PPR points per game to backs over four weeks, and a back has hit 11.8-plus against them in each of their last three. 77 percent rostered on CBS, and CBS says add in all leagues.

items.h: The other must-starts
items.t: Bucky Irving against a Carolina defense allowing the second-most fantasy points to running backs. T.J. Hockenson - double digits in three of his last four, Atlanta allows just under 10 a game to tight ends, and he is the No. 2 target with Addison out. Plus Bijan Robinson, Nico Collins, and the whole Cincinnati passing game at -10 in a 51.5.

items.h: The four fights, and this is the best radio in the segment
items.t: KIRK COUSINS: Bleacher Report says start (Atlanta allows the eighth-most to quarterbacks); CBS says sit (3.8-yard average depth of target, 5.8 yards per attempt against Cover-3, and Atlanta plays single-high at the third-highest rate in the league). Neither accounts for Kyler Murray, limited Wednesday and Thursday. ZACH CHARBONNET: CBS flexes, BR sits. DEEBO SAMUEL: CBS flexes, BR sits - Seattle has allowed the fewest fantasy points to receivers in the league. JAYLEN WARREN: BR starts, CBS calls him risky on six or fewer carries in each of the last two.

items.h: The consensus fade: Mark Andrews at Houston
items.t: Three targets and 3.4 points in his second game with Brissett, and Houston has allowed the fewest fantasy points to tight ends. Both outlets sit him; FantasyPros files him under "droppable, with a chance of regret."

items.h: Fade Jonathan Taylor to flex only
items.t: Eighteen or fewer touches in four straight, and the Giants allowed 1.1 yards per rush against read-option and rank fourth-fewest PPR allowed to backs over four weeks - exactly the look Richardson gives them.

items.h: Quarterback streams, platform named on every number
items.t: Cam Ward at Jacksonville, 37.3 percent on ESPN - 22.5 points a game over four weeks, 19-plus in every game for a month. Geno Smith against Miami, 16.2 percent on ESPN, and he put up 287 and three scores on Miami in Week 7. Deshaun Watson against Las Vegas, 11.1 percent on ESPN but 31 to 32 percent on CBS.

items.h: Defense streams
items.t: Chargers against DeVito, 10 percent on Yahoo. Cleveland against Mendoza, who has taken 11 sacks in two starts, 13 percent on Yahoo. Giants at Indianapolis against Richardson's first start, 16 percent on Yahoo. Note FantasyPros' Denver pick is built on Aaron Rodgers' sack numbers - Rodgers is no longer on the team.

items.h: Stash list update: Antonio Williams has fully graduated
items.t: Nine catches for 122 on 11 targets Monday night, a route on 91.5 percent of dropbacks since the Week 7 bye, second on the team in targets behind Diggs. CBS wants 15 percent-plus of FAAB, the most expensive bid on their board. 21.9 percent on ESPN against 63 on CBS.

items.h: Graduating: Dylan Sampson. Still the best hold: Samaje Perine.
items.t: Sampson is a near 50-50 split with Judkins with 77, 69, 48 and 37 yards in his last four; 19.4 ESPN, 25 Yahoo, 49 CBS, $12 on Yahoo. Perine had 97 total yards Monday night on six carries and four catches, was second on the team in receiving behind Gesicki, has 10-plus touches in three straight, and is in a near-even carry split with Chase Brown. FantasyPros' only explicit stash.

items.h: Cut these two: Kaleb Johnson and Gunnar Helm
items.t: Johnson got eight carries for thirteen yards with Josh Jacobs out, which is as bad as a lead-back day gets. Helm has 21 catches for 183 yards and zero touchdowns through nine games and appears on no Week 12 list anywhere.

items.h: Partial: Konata Mumpfield led all Rams pass-catchers Wednesday - but Stafford threw for 140
items.t: Deep leagues only. Nacua is out for the season and Adams is out to at least Week 13. 9.9 percent on ESPN, 13 Yahoo, 24 CBS.

items.h: New stash, cheapest high ceiling in football: Will Shipley, Philadelphia
items.t: Two percent on Yahoo, four on CBS, $7. Ten carries for 46 yards after Saquon Barkley's third stinger of the season Thursday, and he played every snap after Barkley left.

items.h: Three more new stashes
items.t: Sam Roush, the Chicago tight end - Kmet is out for the year and Loveland was carted off Thursday; Roush went 5-for-5 for 31 and nobody has published a rostership number, so do not make one up. Jack Bech, Las Vegas, 0.3 percent on ESPN, with a route on 77.3 percent of dropbacks and a 21.6 percent target share. And Chris Rodriguez Jr., Jacksonville, at 16.8 percent on ESPN and seventy-two on CBS - the platform gap of the week.

items.h: Never say a percentage without naming the platform
items.t: Sharp Football publishes the INVERSE of rostership - "available in 88.9% of ESPN leagues" means 11.1 percent rostered. CBS runs 20 to 35 points hotter than ESPN on the same player. That is how you tell a caller a 72-percent-owned player is free.

items.h: Items Trent must check Saturday morning
items.t: The Friday designations for all eleven Sunday games and the Monday game - none had posted when this was built, and that is the biggest gap. Colston Loveland's MRI. Purdy. Herbert. Brock Bowers. Derrick Henry, upgraded to full but not formally cleared. Bhayshul Tuten. Tyler Higbee's chest. The Denver-Pittsburgh box score, because Jonah Coleman was CBS's only must-start in it. And whether Aaron Rodgers signed anywhere overnight - he cleared waivers Thursday and was unsigned as of Friday afternoon.

segments.title: Thanksgiving, and it has never happened before

items.h: All three games were won by a go-ahead score inside the final minute - an NFL first on a single day
items.t: That is Elias Sports Bureau. Open with it.

items.h: Bears 39, Lions 35 - Caleb Williams hit Rome Odunze with three seconds left
items.t: Chicago trailed 35-24 in the fourth. Williams 345 to 360 yards depending on the source and two touchdowns, plus a two-point conversion run. Odunze 87 yards and two scores per the Bears' own site. D'Andre Swift 162 scrimmage yards. T.J. Edwards stopped Gibbs on fourth-and-four at the Chicago 32 with 2:17 left.

items.h: Detroit lost anyway despite Jahmyr Gibbs going 21 carries for 205 and three touchdowns
items.t: A 70-yard run was wiped out by penalty. 1,007 combined yards is the second-most in a Thanksgiving game, and Chicago's 549 allowed is its most in a non-overtime game since 1982. The Lions are 1-9 in their last ten Thanksgivings. Chicago took sole possession of first in the NFC North. Bears tight end Colston Loveland was carted off with a knee injury.

items.h: Eagles 39, Cowboys 38 - Jake Elliott won it with two seconds left from 59 or 60 yards
items.t: Sources disagree on the distance. Philadelphia erased a 21-point third-quarter deficit at 31-10. Joe Milton, starting for Jalen Hurts, went 21-of-31 for 331 with three touchdown passes and a rushing score.

items.h: DeVonta Smith caught 11 of 14 targets for 200 yards and two touchdowns
items.t: A career high, on scores of 50 and 45. ESPN lists 186 yards; CBS's line is the more specific one.

items.h: The play and the decision that swung it
items.t: A blocked punt returned for a touchdown by Kenny Moore II off a Ty Robinson block. And leading by two with 55 seconds left, Brian Schottenheimer went for it on fourth-and-one from the Philadelphia 39 and Prescott was sacked. Javonte Williams had three rushing touchdowns, all in the first half. Goedert out with a shoulder, DeJean in concussion protocol, and Saquon Barkley treated for a stinger - his third of the season - finishing with five carries for seven yards. Eagles 4-7, Cowboys 5-7.

items.h: Bills 13, Chiefs 10 - Tyler Bass from 57 as time expired, and Josh Allen was awful
items.t: Set up by a partially blocked punt with fifteen seconds left returned by Greg Dortch to the Kansas City 39. Allen went 10-of-21 for 81 yards with two interceptions, both in the red zone, and an 18.3 passer rating. Mahomes 16-of-29 for 174. Rain, low 30s at Highmark. Harrison Butker missed from 46 with six minutes left. Bills 10-1 on a seven-game streak; Chiefs 8-3 and now behind Denver in the AFC West.

items.h: James Cook III tied Terry Allen's thirty-year-old record - tied, not broke
items.t: Ten straight games with 75-plus rushing yards and a rushing touchdown. ESPN's recap calls it a record set; Yahoo and SB Nation say tied. He cannot break it this week - Buffalo has already played. Emmett Johnson scored for the fifth straight game, the first Chiefs rookie to do it.

items.h: And Wednesday: Rams 26, Packers 13 on Netflix, the first Thanksgiving Eve game ever played
items.t: Blake Corum went 32 carries for a career-high 184 and a score. CBS reports the league intends to make the Wednesday game annual.

segments.title: Week 11 rewind, and the record that did not fall

items.h: Joe Burrow tied Peyton Manning and did not pass him
items.t: He went 28-of-40 for 300 with two touchdowns - not four - so the streak ended at five straight games with four-plus. The record is shared, not broken, and several Nov 23 preview pieces are still live with "Burrow can break it tonight" headlines.

items.h: Commanders 22, Bengals 20 on a walk-off
items.t: McPherson hit a 56-yarder to put Cincinnati up 20-19 inside the last minute, Jayden Daniels moved Washington down the field in two plays, and Drew Stevens hit a 26-yarder as time expired. Zac Taylor: "Those last two drives are what got us."

items.h: Sunday night in Mexico City was a rout: 49ers 35, Vikings 10
items.t: San Francisco was -3 with a 46.5 - covered easily, and well under.

items.h: The rest of Week 11
items.t: Bills 26, Dolphins 9. Panthers 35, Ravens 33. Bears 21, Saints 13. Cowboys 51, Titans 30. Lions 31, Buccaneers 21. Chiefs 34, Cardinals 7. Eagles 19, Steelers 16. Jets 27, Chargers 24. Giants 23, Jaguars 18. Broncos 38, Raiders 24. Thursday was Texans 26, Colts 3. Six teams were on bye: Atlanta, Cleveland, Green Bay, the Rams, New England and Seattle.

segments.title: Where things stand after Thanksgiving

items.h: AFC seeds, and Denver is the two seed at 8-2 ahead of an 8-3 Kansas City
items.t: 1 Bills 10-1, 2 Broncos 8-2, 3 Jaguars 7-3, 4 Bengals 7-3, wild cards Chiefs 8-3, Browns 6-4, Steelers 6-4. Denver holds it on head-to-head in common games, and an 8-3 Chiefs team is a wild card. In the hunt: Patriots 5-5, Texans 4-6, Raiders 4-7, Ravens 4-7, Jets 3-8.

items.h: NFC seeds, and the oddity is worse than last week
items.t: 1 49ers 9-1, 2 Bears 9-2, 3 Giants 6-3-1, 4 Panthers 5-5, wild cards Lions 8-3, Vikings 7-3, Rams 7-4. Detroit is 8-3 and sitting fifth, behind a 5-5 Carolina team with a home playoff game. In the hunt: Seahawks 6-4, Packers 6-5, Commanders 4-5-1, Cowboys 5-7, Eagles 4-7. One conflict: SI lists the Raiders 4-6 where NBC has 4-7; NBC's table is internally consistent.

items.h: Nobody can clinch anything this week - no berth, no division, no top seed
items.t: Pro Football Network says it flatly. If a caller says otherwise, they are wrong.

items.h: Divisional eliminations are live, though
items.t: The Jets can be eliminated from the AFC East, the Chargers from the AFC West, and the Titans and Colts from the AFC South.

items.h: Probabilities as of Nov 24
items.t: Bills and 49ers both above 99 percent to make it. Broncos 99. Chiefs 99 but only 44 percent to win the AFC West. Jaguars 98, Bengals 97, Steelers 62, Browns 56.

blocks.title: Block 3: Week 12 Picks, the Vegas Numbers and the Locks

segments.title: The board - and there are no NFL games today

items.h: Week 12's Saturday is empty
items.t: nfl.com and ESPN both list games Wednesday, Thursday, Friday, Sunday and Monday - and nothing on Saturday Nov 28. The league's Saturday doubleheaders start in December. Everything below is tomorrow and Monday.

items.h: 1:00 PM Sunday
items.t: Saints at Bengals, CBS, Cincinnati -10 with a 51.5, the highest total on the board. Ravens at Texans, CBS, Houston -6.5, 46.5. Jets at Dolphins, CBS, New York -3.5, 41.5. Giants at Colts, FOX, New York -6.5, 41.5. Falcons at Vikings, FOX, Minnesota -6.5, 42.5. Titans at Jaguars, FOX, Jacksonville -14.5 with a 47.5 - the biggest spread of the week.

items.h: Afternoon and primetime
items.t: Patriots at Chargers, 4:05 CBS, Los Angeles -1.5 with a 36.5 on this board. Commanders at Cardinals, 4:25 FOX, Washington -7, 41.5. Seahawks at 49ers, 4:25 FOX, San Francisco -3, 47.5 - FOX's A-team game with Burkhardt, Brady and Andrews. Raiders at Browns, Sunday 8:20 NBC, Cleveland -4.5, 40.5. Panthers at Buccaneers, Monday 8:15 ESPN, Tampa Bay -3, 43.5.

items.h: The line move of the week is a six-point swing that flipped the favorite
items.t: Patriots at Chargers opened Los Angeles -3.5 and is now New England -2.5, with the total down from 39.5 to 35.5. The driver is Justin Herbert's concussion, with DeVito starting on the other side. Both quarterbacks in that game are backups.

items.h: Also moved
items.t: Seahawks-49ers' total dropped three, from 46.5 to 43.5, on Purdy's ankle. Jets-Dolphins moved two toward the Jets to -5.5. New Orleans-Cincinnati's total came down two to 49.5. The movement source does not name a book, so treat the direction as real and the exact numbers as directional.

items.h: Say the caveat: this DraftKings board is Wednesday-morning vintage
items.t: And where other boards disagree, do not blend them. FOX via bet365 has Cincinnati -9.5 with a 49.5, the Jets -5.5, San Francisco -2.5 with a 44.5. Sharp Football's consensus is four days stale and still carries last week's Bengals-Commanders game in its Week 12 table.

segments.title: Sunday Night Football: Raiders at Browns, 8:20 NBC

items.h: Cleveland -4.5 with a 40.5, a total that has not moved all week
items.t: Cleveland is 6-4 and holding the AFC's sixth seed, off a bye. Las Vegas is 4-7 and done.

items.h: Cris Collinsworth is not on this game
items.t: He takes his customary post-Thanksgiving break three nights after doing Chiefs-Bills, and Jason Garrett fills in alongside Tirico and Melissa Stark - as Garrett did in the same slot in 2023.

items.h: The fantasy angle and the betting angle are the same angle
items.t: Fernando Mendoza, the No. 1 overall pick, has taken eleven sacks in two starts, is off-target on 19.7 percent of his throws since taking over, and Cleveland leads the league in man coverage and single-high looks. That is why the Browns defense is a top-two stream at 13 percent on Yahoo.

items.h: Brock Bowers was limited Thursday on the ankle and the team is optimistic
items.t: Practice status only - no designation.

segments.title: Monday Night Football: Panthers at Buccaneers, 8:15 ESPN

items.h: Tampa Bay -3 with a 43.5, moved from -2.5
items.t: Buck and Aikman, with Salters and Rutledge. Yahoo also lists an ABC simulcast.

items.h: This is the NFC South title game in miniature, and the records make no sense
items.t: Carolina is 5-5 and holds the NFC's four seed and a home playoff game. Tampa Bay is 3-7 and nfl.com's model still gave the Buccaneers a 29 percent chance to win the division as of Nov 24. A 3-7 team is one game from the postseason because of what division it is in.

items.h: Bryce Young was listed full "in the estimate" - and Carolina did not practice
items.t: An estimate on a non-practice day is the weakest signal there is. Say so if you use it.

items.h: Fantasy crossover
items.t: Bucky Irving is a must-start here because Carolina has allowed the second-most fantasy points to running backs, and Baker Mayfield is a sit on a thin target group in an expected run-heavy script.

segments.title: The Vegas numbers - implied team totals

items.h: These are our numbers, not published figures, and the arithmetic has been verified in code
items.t: Computed off the DraftKings board above, Nov 26. Favorite is total plus spread over two; underdog is total minus spread over two.

items.t: Jaguars 31.0 / Titans 16.5. Bengals 30.75 / Saints 20.75. Texans 26.5 / Ravens 20.0. 49ers 25.25 / Seahawks 22.25. Vikings 24.5 / Falcons 18.0. Commanders 24.25 / Cardinals 17.25. Giants 24.0 / Colts 17.5. Buccaneers 23.25 / Panthers 20.25. Jets 22.5 / Dolphins 19.0. Browns 22.5 / Raiders 18.0. Chargers 19.0 / Patriots 17.5.

items.h: Highest: Jacksonville at 31.0, just ahead of Cincinnati at 30.75
items.t: Those two are the only teams on the board above 27 - a 14.5-point favorite in a 47.5 game and a 10-point favorite in a 51.5.

items.h: Lowest: Tennessee at 16.5, and then a cluster
items.t: Arizona 17.25, Indianapolis and New England tied at 17.5. Nothing as extreme as Arizona's 12.0 two weeks ago, but four teams under 18 is the most crowded bottom we have had.

items.h: Start both sides: Saints-Bengals and Seahawks-49ers
items.t: Saints-Bengals at 30.75 and 20.75 is the only game with a side above 27, and Seahawks-49ers at 25.25 and 22.25 is the only one where both teams clear 22. That is the game to build lineups around.

items.h: Patriots-Chargers is the one to show your work on, because the live number inverts it
items.t: On Wednesday's board it is Chargers 19.0 and Patriots 17.5. On the current New England -2.5 with a 35.5 it becomes Patriots 19.0 and Chargers 16.5 - the favorite flips and Los Angeles becomes the lowest implied total on the whole board. Two backup quarterbacks and a 35.5 total: use the defenses, not the lineups, which is exactly why the Chargers and Patriots defenses are both top-four streams.

items.h: Two more off the live numbers, plus the standing caution
items.t: Seahawks-49ers on the 43.5 becomes 49ers 23.25 / Seahawks 20.25. Saints-Bengals on the 49.5 becomes Bengals 29.75 / Saints 19.75. And four of these totals sit at 41.5 or lower - one point of total movement moves two implied numbers by half a point each. Re-check before you build anything on them.

segments.title: Locks of the week and the close

items.h: One NFL play and one sentence from each panelist
items.t: Name the book and say the NFL board here is Wednesday's.

items.h: The close, and hit all six
items.t: There are no NFL games today, so everything we picked is tomorrow and Monday. The Patriots-Chargers line has flipped six points and both quarterbacks in that game are backups. There are still no official injury designations on any Sunday or Monday game, so nobody says "questionable" on the air. Anthony Richardson has the Colts and Mason Rudolph has Pittsburgh - and circle back to the top of the show, because Aaron Rodgers cleared waivers Thursday and was still unsigned. Nobody clinches anything this week, and a 5-5 Carolina team is still ahead of an 8-3 Detroit team. And Joe Burrow tied Peyton Manning and did not pass him.

items.h: Tease next week
items.t: The fifth CFP rankings Tuesday, Conference Championship Saturday on Dec 5, the final twelve-team bracket on Sunday Dec 6, whether West Virginia got to six wins last night, and four teams on bye in NFL Week 13 - Baltimore, Indianapolis, Las Vegas and the Jets.
